summary: Modular monolith: Spring Boot + Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL serving React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS, hosted on AWS ECS on Fargate (ap-south-1 Mumbai). Estimated $1,150-4,850/month (within the $6,000 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable with strict internal modules for the fintech domain (e.g. ledger, loans, KYC, payments): a 8-engineer team gets clear boundaries without distributed-system overhead; modules can be extracted later if scale demands it. The ML model is deployed as a separate service so it can be retrained and scaled independently. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 8 engineer(s) cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.choice: React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS
frontend.justification: Web - React + Vite (SPA): Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); shares React/TypeScript skills and code with the React Native (Expo) app; rich client-side interactivity for a fintech; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=2. Mobile - React Native (Expo): Chosen because one codebase ships both Android and iOS (project.platforms); team already works in typescript (team.languages); strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=4.

alternatives.why_not: React + Vite scores higher on cost (fit 6.8 vs 6.9).

warnings.message: ISO 27001/SOC 2 certify your controls, not the stack: providers with attestations were chosen so you inherit their controls, but you still need policies, access reviews and audits.
CERT-In Directions (2022): keep ICT system logs for 180 days within Indian jurisdiction.
DPDP Act 2023: consent notices, purpose limitation, breach intimation to the Data Protection Board and erasure on request. India residency is enforced because data_residency=india.
PCI DSS: use the gateway's hosted checkout/tokenisation so card data never touches your servers (SAQ A scope); only PCI-attested providers were selected.
RBI data localisation: all payment-system data stays in Indian regions; if any processing happens abroad, the data must be deleted there and returned to India within one business day/24 hours.
